Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

successful adjective

of an attempt or a plan: turning out as hoped

also succeed, successfully, it worked, turn out well, go well

classical

Liv. praef. 13: successūs prosperōs
Cic. Att. 9.7.1: prosperōs exitūs

prosperus (prosper), prospera, prosperum

adjective

successful, favourable, as one hoped

With a verb: prosperē ēvenīre, prosperē prōcēdere, to turn out well (Liv. 23.27.12; Cic. Fam. 12.9.2; Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • succēdō, succēdere, successī, successum — to be successful, to work, to go well (of a thing attempted)

    verb, third conjugation, intransitive; in this sense mostly in the third person · classical · Ter. And. 670: hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā; Caes. BG 7.26: quod rēs nūlla successerat (Lewis & Short)

    Latin says “it succeeded” where English says “it was successful”.

  • prōcēdō, prōcēdere, prōcessī, prōcessum — to turn out well, to succeed

    verb, third conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 12.9.2: omnia prosperē prōcēdent (Lewis & Short)

  • fēlīx, fēlīcis — successful, lucky

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 5.40: et bene et fēlīciter gesta (Lewis & Short); Traupman 387: success, rēs fēlīciter gesta

    Successfully is fēlīciter; a success, rēs fēlīciter or bene gesta (Traupman 387).

Examples

  • Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.

    I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out. … It didn’t work this way; we’ll go at it by another road.Ter. And. 669–670

  • ut ōrsīs tantum operis successūs prosperōs darent

    that they might grant success to so great a work now begunLiv. praef. 13

See also successful, positive, good luck!, success.
